summary: Feed s116_double is degraded: 82.3% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS 60% tolerance and 1.56 Gbps bursts overload the 1 Gbps IDS port (156% capacity), causing payload blindness and packet loss risk.

findings.root_cause: 82.3% of bytes are TLS-encrypted vs 60% IDS tolerance; packet broker is forwarding encrypted traffic without SSL visibility/decryption, so payloads remain opaque.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload inspection but cannot match signatures or detect malware/C2/exfiltration inside encrypted flows, severely reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: IDS is payload-dependent; decrypting relevant TLS at the broker or providing decrypted copy/metadata restores inspection capability without exceeding tool design limits.

findings.root_cause: Peak burst 1.56 Gbps in 1ms intervals exceeds 1 Gbps IDS port capacity (156% utilization, 4 overloaded intervals); broker is sending unshaped bursts without load balancing or filtering.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port oversubscribed will drop packets during bursts, causing incomplete flows, missed signatures, and attacker evasion via burst-induced loss.

recommended_fix.why: Distributing traffic across 2x1G IDS ports or adding filtering keeps per-port load below 80% threshold and prevents burst drops while preserving both directions for stateful inspection.
